title: Severe flooding
description: The 1-in-100-year storm tide at 2040 sea level (1.8 m AHD), the event Melbourne Water uses to assess safe pedestrian access in Southbank, with full stormwater ponding. A static estimate, not a hydraulic model: no flow or velocity. Upstream river flows can raise Southbank levels above the bay tide level, so river depths are a lower bound.
sources: Mechanism: Melbourne Water, Southbank Precinct Local Floodplain Development Plan (2026). Safe pedestrian access is assessed for the 1% AEP flood with a 2040 planning horizon.

River level: Melbourne Water 1% annual exceedance probability tide level in Port Phillip Bay, Planning for Sea Level Rise Guidelines (2017), as cited in GHD (2019) Appendix G, Fishermans Bend flood levee memo. 2040: 1.8 m AHD.

Stormwater ponding: closed depressions of the ground model, anywhere in the area; the plan describes local stormwater flooding as shallow but widespread across streets, laneways and building interfaces.
Ground: Geoscience Australia 5 m LiDAR digital elevation model (CC BY 4.0).
